full_judgment: 22. It appears from different statutes that the confiscation has also been used : such as in section 24 of the Arms Act, 1878. There is a provision for confiscation at the discretion of the Courts or Tribunals in the event of an offence in respect of any arms, ammunitions or military stores, similarly, section 55(1) of the Forest Act, 1927 entails confiscation of all timber of forest produced in respect of an offence under the said section of the Act is committed including all tools, boat, vehicles used in committing any forest offence. Similarly, section 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 provision for confiscation of the property in possession of an offender proved to be disproportionate to his known sources of income, section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 in connection with the offence of criminal misconduct by a public servant the pecuniary sources or property to which the criminal misconduct relates may also be confiscated to the State, section 9 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 contemplates confiscation of whole or any part of the property of the accused to the government charged before the Special Judge with an offence triable under the Act. Similar Provision for “বাজেয়াপ্তকরন” is available under section 33 and 34 of the Narcotics Control Act, 1990, section 33B of Bangladesh Standard and Testing Institute Ordinance, 1985 also contemplates confiscation of the article or any other things in respect of which or by which any offence under this Ordinance has been committed, section 23 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947 also contemplates confiscation of any currency, security, gold or silver of goods or other property in respect of which the contravention of the provision of this Act has taken place, section 5A of the Protection and Conservation of Fish Act, 1950 also contemplates confiscation of any article or thing used or intended to be used in the commission of an offence punishable under this Act or the Rules made under this Act, section 156 of the Customs Act, 1969 contemplates confiscation of goods connected with the offence in addition to the sentence when any one committed any offence described in the Schedule of the said Act.
